text:

title: Homework 2
text:
Task 1: Basic Vector Practice
Suppose we have data from a medical experiment on blood pressure.

Create two vectors. One vector corresponding to the pre-treatment values for subjects 1 through 20 and one vector corresponding to the post-treatment values for subjects 1 through 20.


#assign values to pre_treatment
pre_treatment <- c(130, 128, 116, 124, 133, 134, 118, 126, 114, 127, 141, 138, 128, 140, 137, 131, 120, 128, 139, 135)

#assign values to post_treatment
post_treatment <- c(114, 98, 113, 99, 107, 116, 113, 111, 119, 117, 101, 119, 130, 122, 106, 106, 124, 102, 117, 113)

#view results
pre_treatment

 [1] 130 128 116 124 133 134 118 126 114 127 141 138 128 140 137 131 120 128 139
[20] 135

post_treatment

 [1] 114  98 113  99 107 116 113 111 119 117 101 119 130 122 106 106 124 102 117
[20] 113



Assign names to the vector elements using the paste() function.


#assign names
names(pre_treatment) <- paste("Subject", 1:20, sep = "_")
names(post_treatment) <- paste("Subject", 1:20, sep = "_")

#view results
pre_treatment

 Subject_1  Subject_2  Subject_3  Subject_4  Subject_5  Subject_6  Subject_7 
       130        128        116        124        133        134        118 
 Subject_8  Subject_9 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_13 Subject_14 
       126        114        127        141        138        128        140 
Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
       137        131        120        128        139        135

 Subject_8  Subject_9 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_13 Subject_14 
       111        119        117        101        119        130        122 
Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
       106        106        124        102        117        113 



Calculate the change in blood pressure for each patient by subtracting post-treatment measurements from pre-treatment measurements.


#calculate change in blood pressure
blood_pressure_change <- pre_treatment - post_treatment

#view results
blood_pressure_change

 Subject_1  Subject_2  Subject_3  Subject_4  Subject_5  Subject_6  Subject_7

        15         -5         10         40         19         -2         18 
Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
        31         25         -4         26         22         22 



Calculate the average decrease in blood pressure accross all patients.


mean(blood_pressure_change)

[1] 17



Determine which patients experienced a decrease in blood pressure after treatment (a positive change). Use the which() function to just return the indices (and names) associated with this type of change.


which(blood_pressure_change > 0)

Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20

#subset the vector
blood_pressure_decreased <- blood_pressure_change[blood_pressure_change > 0]

#view results
blood_pressure_decreased

mean(blood_pressure_decreased)

Task 3: List Practice
Continue the previous example. Suppose we now have another experiment where the “treatment” was actually a placebo.

Create a new data frame for the placebo data.

#calculate blood pressure changes

patient_list[[1]]$status <- character(20)
#fill the status column with post treatment bp rating
for (i in 1:20) {
  if (patient_list[[1]][i, 3] <= 120) {
    patient_list[[1]][i,6] <- "Optimal"
  } 
  else if (patient_list[[1]][i, 3] <= 130) {patient_list[[1]][i,6] <- "Borderline"
  } 
  else {
    patient_list[[1]][i,6] <- "High"
  }
}
